page.running_head: AD PSALM. XV. DE VSVRA APPENDIX.

main_text.l: Sed tandem finem istis de Vsura considerationibus imponimus. Nam, sicut initiò memini, plane potest stultitiæ deputari, pluribus occupari in re tali, quæ more podagræ, nullas admit-tit medicas manus. Malum hoc vsqueadeo inualuit, vt post multorum bonorum virorum admonitionem factum sit incurabile. Nam ipsos vertices corripuit, quorum erat authoritate sua eiusmodi corruptionibus occurrere, & subiecta membra in studio verae iustitiae dirigere ac moderari. Dictum Christi est: Si sal infatuatus fuerit, in quo salietur? Item: Vos estis lux Mundi. Si lumen quod in vobis est, caliginosum fuerit, corporis caligo quanta erit? Reliquum est, vt expectemus manum Domini: qui breui est omnis generis corruptelas de Ecclesia sua subláturus. Is tandem veniat, & suos liberet.

page.notes: The text starts with "Sed", so it probably continues from the previous page, and I have marked it cont="true". "subláturus" may carry an accent over the a; I read it as printed but it is uncertain. The question mark after "salietur" and the hyphen in "admit-" and "ad-" are as I read them. The woodcut ornament (a putto between scrolls, with a mask at the bottom) has no printed text. Faint show-through of the other side of the leaf appears in the lower half of the page and is left out.
